prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Houston for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” dentist for implants in Houston — the right provider depends on your needs (single tooth vs. full-arch, bone loss or grafting needed, sedation needs, budget, insurance, etc.). That said, here’s how to find the best implant clinician for you and what to look for.

Who places implants
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMFS): do surgery and complex cases (bone grafts, IV sedation).
- Periodontists: specialists in gums and implant placement, good for grafts and esthetics.
- Prosthodontists: specialists in restoring teeth and implant crowns/bridges — excellent for complex restorative work and full‑arch cases.
- Some general dentists with advanced implant training also place implants.

How to evaluate providers
- Relevant specialty and board certification (ABOMS for OMFS, American Board of Periodontology, American Board of Prosthodontics).
- Years of experience and number of implants placed yearly.
- Advanced training/courses in implantology and use of modern technology (CBCT 3D imaging, guided surgery).
- Before/after photos of cases similar to yours and patient references.
- Use of reputable implant systems (Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Zimmer/BioHorizons, etc.).
- Clear treatment plan, timeline, total cost, and warranty/guarantee on restorations.
- Good reviews on multiple platforms (Google, Healthgrades, Yelp) — but read details, not just ratings.
- Comfortable office environment and whether they coordinate care (surgery + restoration) if multiple specialists are involved.

Questions to ask at a consult
- How many implants like mine have you placed?
- Are you board-certified or fellowship-trained?
- Will you need bone grafting/sinus lift? How long to finish treatment?
- Who will make the crown/prosthesis? (same doctor or another specialist)
- What implant system do you use and why?
- Can I see before/after photos and patient testimonials?
- What are the full fees and payment/finance options?
- What sedation options do you provide?

Where to search/trustworthy resources
- AAOMS (American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons) directory
- American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) dentist locator
- American College of Prosthodontists / American Academy of Periodontology directories
- ADA Find-a-Dentist + local reviews

If you want, I can:
- Look up highly rated implant specialists in Houston in a specific ZIP code or neighborhood,
- Compare 3–5 dentists/clinics and give contact info, specialties, and patient-review summaries.

Tell me your ZIP code and any preferences (insurance, sedation, single tooth vs full-arch) and I’ll pull a short list.
